scope: s2c payload decoding for the ten user-listed Lua-bound inbound receiver opcodes
offsetBasis: fields[] offsets are application-payload relative, after the 16-byte game-message prefix. The PCAP-derived mirror layouts keep full game-message body offsets separately.

s2c_0x013d.name: SetActorNamePacket
s2c_0x013d.offsetBasis: application payload offsets after the 16-byte game-message prefix; s2c SubPacket source/target header fields are not included in fields[]

fields.name: displayNameId
fields.note: Constructor normalizes incoming zero to 0xffffffff before writing the CharaBase+0x60 display-name sub-struct.

fields.name: customName
fields.note: The client wrapper copies the full 0x20-byte name area before string construction.

fields.name: displayNameKind
fields.note: The dword at payload+0x24; isSexMale; the client stores it; the display-name kind selector.

receiverVariants.note: Wrapper reads displayNameId, copies payload+4..0x23 as the custom-name string, and passes payload+0x24 low byte to the receiver constructor.

s2c_0x013d.notes: These receiver decompilations often parse packet bytes into short-lived CommandInterface receiver objects before the apply method mutates actor fields. fields[] records the wire application payload layout; receiverVariants preserve the constructor/apply evidence.

observations: Most small s2c receivers split into a wrapper/constructor that reads packet bytes and an apply method that mutates actor fields from receiver storage.
SetActorNamePacket carries a 40-byte application payload: u32 displayNameId, 0x20-byte name area, and a low-byte display-name kind at payload+0x24.
Achievement points, but the client applies only the low u32.
SetCurrentJob's receiver applies only the low u8 into PlayerBase+0xf1.
SetActorIconPacket is a packed u32 flag word; the known AFK, disconnecting, and GM bits match the receiver's CharaBase+0xdc+0x10 net-stat storage.
SetActorStatusAllPacket is the wide 20*u16 status-id block; the receiver chain converts entries into dynamic CharaBase+0xdc status-array writes.
